title: Lack of Authentication for Student Login
description: Student may submit assignments without proper authentication, allowing unauthorized access to the system.
assumptions: Assumes student identity verification is required before submission.

title: Unintended Data Collection During Login
description: Student login process may inadvertently collect additional personal information beyond required fields.
assumptions: Assumes login form may include optional fields that capture extra data.

title: Inadequate Access Control for Grades Portal
description: Grades Portal may have insufficient access controls allowing unauthorized users to view or modify student submissions.
assumptions: Assumes access control mechanisms exist but may be inadequate.

title: Potential Data Disclosure of Student Information
description: Student personal data (student ID, course, submission timestamp) may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the Grades Portal.
assumptions: Assumes data is stored and potentially accessible by unauthorized parties.

title: Data Integrity Risk for Submitted Assignments
description: Submitted assignment data may be altered, corrupted, or lost during processing by the Grades Portal.
assumptions: Assumes data integrity mechanisms may not be fully implemented.

title: Student identifier transmitted to grading service
description: The Grades Portal Web App transmits student ID to the Assignment & Grading Service, which contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject. This identifier enables tracking and profiling of individual students across the system.
assumptions: Student ID is transmitted in clear or encrypted form as part of the submission request.

title: Processing of identified data at portal
description: The Grades Portal Web App requests and processes identified data (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) before routing to the Assignment & Grading Service. This processing of identifying information creates privacy risks.
assumptions: The portal collects and processes these data elements as part of the submission workflow.

title: Non-repudiation of student submissions
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives student submissions and grades. Students may be unable to deny their involvement in the submission process or the grading outcome, as the system creates evidence linking them to specific actions.
assumptions: The system maintains records of who submitted what and when.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role. This enables linking of student data across different systems and potentially across time, creating linkability risks.
assumptions: Student ID is used as a key to link data across the system.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Assignment Storage
description: The grading service stores student ID, course, and submission time. This may collect more personal data than strictly necessary for the assignment grading function, violating the minimality principle.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure via Metadata
description: The assignment file may contain implicit personal data (e.g., file creation time, metadata) that is disclosed to the data store without explicit consent or necessity.

title: Data Loss During Storage
description: The assignment store may experience data loss or corruption, resulting in loss of student assignment records.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignments
description: The assignment store may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of student assignment data.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Retention Requirements
description: The assignment store may retain student data beyond required retention periods, violating data protection regulations.

title: Teacher's login credentials processed for identification
description: The teacher's login credentials are processed by the system to identify and authenticate the teacher before granting access to course submission queues. This processing could potentially expose or leak identifying information about the teacher.
assumptions: The system processes the teacher's credentials to identify them as a legitimate user with access to specific courses.

title: Teacher may access unauthorized course submissions
description: The teacher may request submission queues for courses they are not authorized to review, potentially accessing student data they should not have access to.
assumptions: The system may not properly validate the teacher's course enrollment or permission before granting access to submission queues.

title: Submission data potentially leaked during teacher access
description: When the teacher requests the queue of submissions, the system may inadvertently expose student submission data to unauthorized parties or through improper data handling during the request process.
assumptions: The system processes and transmits student submission data to the teacher, which could be intercepted or mishandled.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Information
description: Student submissions (names, work content, submission times) may be disclosed to unauthorized teachers or parties without proper access controls.

title: Information Loss During Transmission
description: Student data may be lost or corrupted during transmission from the portal to the teacher, potentially affecting data integrity and availability.

title: Unintended Data Exposure
description: The data flow may expose more student information than intended, such as submission times revealing patterns or work content being used for purposes other than assessment.

title: Teacher credentials exposed during login
description: Teacher's login credentials or identity could be intercepted or exposed during the authentication process when accessing the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Assumes standard web authentication is used

title: Student information leaked to unauthorized parties
description: Student identifiers and grade information could be leaked to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Assumes standard data transmission protocols

title: Teacher non-repudiation of grade submission
description: Teacher could deny having submitted the grade and feedback, as there may be no secure audit trail or digital signature.
assumptions: Assumes no digital signature or audit mechanism

title: Data integrity compromised during transmission
description: Grade and feedback data could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission from Teacher to Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Assumes no encryption or integrity checks

title: Unauthorized access to grade data
description: Unauthorized users could access the grade and feedback data stored in the Grades Portal Web App without proper authorization controls.
assumptions: Assumes standard access controls

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records
description: Grade records containing sensitive student information (student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, timestamp) may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data store is not properly secured or if the process writes data without proper access controls.

title: Unauthorized access to grade records
description: The grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized users who could view, modify, or exfiltrate sensitive student grade information.

title: Loss or destruction of grade records
description: Grade records may be lost or destroyed due to data corruption, system failure, or malicious deletion, resulting in permanent loss of student grade information.

title: Unavailability of grade records
description: Grade records may become unavailable due to system failures, maintenance, or attacks, preventing authorized users from accessing student grades when needed.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades
description: Grades and teacher feedback displayed to the student could be accessed by unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, unauthorized personnel) who should not have visibility into this sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Assumes the portal has appropriate access controls to restrict viewing to the student only.

title: Unauthorized viewing of student data
description: The portal may allow unauthorized users to view the student's grades and feedback without proper authentication or authorization mechanisms.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on user authentication to control access to the displayed information.

title: Data integrity of displayed grades
description: The grades and teacher feedback displayed to the student could be tampered with or modified before display, potentially leading to inaccurate information being shown to the student.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow from the data store to the portal is protected from unauthorized modification.

title: Unauthorized access to parent account
description: Parent's login credentials could be intercepted or stolen during the authentication process, allowing unauthorized access to the system.

title: Lack of confidentiality for credentials
description: Parent's login credentials transmitted during authentication may be exposed to network eavesdroppers.

title: Information leakage of child grades
description: Child's grades data could be exposed to unauthorized parties during the request processing.

title: Data integrity of grades
description: Child's grades data could be tampered with during storage or transmission, compromising accuracy.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades to unauthorized parties
description: The portal may disclose grades, feedback, and submission history to unauthorized parties (e.g., other parents, school staff without permission) through the display mechanism.

title: Unauthorized access to portal by non-parent users
description: The portal may be accessed by unauthorized users (e.g., other parents, students, or malicious actors) who should not have access to the child's personal information.

title: Data loss during transmission to parent
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may be lost or corrupted during transmission from the portal to the parent's device or network.

title: Unintended disclosure of sibling or other students' information
description: The portal may inadvertently display information about other students or siblings that should remain private, due to insufficient access controls or data segregation.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The portal may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding the sharing of student information with parents, including consent requirements and data minimization.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: Account records containing sensitive user information (e.g., student identifiers, grades, parent-child relationships) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the write operation to the account directory.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory is accessible to unauthorized entities

title: Loss of Account Records During Write Operation
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links could be lost or corrupted during the write operation to the account directory, resulting in data integrity issues.
assumptions: Assumes the write operation may fail or be interrupted

title: Unintended Consequences of Account Data Write
description: The write operation could have unintended consequences, such as writing incorrect, incomplete, or outdated account records to the directory.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service may not always write accurate data

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The write operation to the account directory may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding the handling of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service handles personal data without explicit compliance measures

title: Unnecessary Data Disclosure to Third Party
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider, potentially exceeding minimum data requirements for backup/replication purposes.
assumptions: Assumes backup/replication requires full data transfer rather than selective or encrypted transfer.

title: Data Leakage During Transfer
description: Personal data transferred to third-party cloud provider may be exposed during transmission or accessed by unauthorized parties at the hosting provider.
assumptions: Assumes data is transferred without adequate encryption or access controls.

title: Data Retention Beyond Necessity
description: Cloud hosting provider may retain full grade records, assignments, and account directory beyond the retention period required for backup purposes, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes cloud provider follows standard retention policies that may exceed minimum requirements.

title: Unauthorized Grade Record Disclosure
description: Grade records may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the flow from DataStore to Process. Without proper access controls, sensitive student information could be exposed to unauthorized users accessing the grading service.

title: Inadequate Access Control for Grade Records
description: Access controls for grade records may be inadequate, allowing unauthorized personnel to access student grades during the data flow to the grading service.

title: Lack of Data Encryption in Transit
description: Grade records may not be encrypted during transmission from DataStore to Process, exposing sensitive student information during the data flow.

title: Inadequate View Access Controls
description: The grading service may build student, parent, and teacher views without adequate access controls, potentially exposing grade information to unauthorized users.

title: Unintended Data Exposure in View Generation
description: During view generation for students, parents, and teachers, unintended data exposure may occur if access controls are not properly implemented.
